grading.explanation:
The new marks are wrong for both changed moves.

Move 15 A14 (correct now, wrong after the fixes; its child W A18 flips with it) and move 15 F19 (correct now, wrong after the fixes): neither is worse than E16. They lose their mark only because the sibling leaf E16 still has the old S[A-1KO], which besogo reads as A-1KO+. That leaf has the same error the research fixed on the other two leaves. After E16, White takes at A18 at once, and Black must retake with a threat (if it doesn't, B19 captures four stones and White lives). Black then needs one approach, and after it White retakes first for free. So E16 is A-1KO- at best, never A-1KO+.

E16 is in fact the weaker of the three. White can never extend at E16, so Black should keep that liberty for the final capture. Played first, E16 leaves A14 and F19, and White can extend at either. Whichever one Black leaves for last, White extends there when it is in atari: at A14 it gets A13 and B14, at F19 it gets F18 and G19. Black must answer, White retakes for free, and Black needs a third threat. That makes E16 A-1KO-2.

After A14 or F19, Black approaches at the other extendable liberty and captures at E16 with its second threat, so those two are A-1KO-. In the wider area, every one-threat case for E16 that was decided fails and two threats win, while the siblings win with one.

By the full count (narrow area) all three moves need 4 threats more than White: E16 needs 4, F19 needs 4, A14 needs 4 by the checker's label run (3 or 4 in my own runs). So under no reading is E16 better than A14 or F19, and rejecting them is wrong.

What the right grading is depends on the owner's labels:
- E16 leaf set to A-1KO-2 (his approach rule): besogo keeps A14 and F19 correct and marks only E16 wrong.
- E16 leaf set to A-1KO- (same as the others): no mark changes.

Which one turns on the open approach-label decision (the label by structure against the full count, and his approach-round rule from c121).

A side note for the report: the research's own key lines for k027 and k028 use E16 as the approach. That is the wrong order: with no threat left White extends at the remaining liberty and Black fails. The A-1KO- labels still stand through the other approach (A14 for k027, F19 for k028), and the diagrams should use those.

reviews.explanation:
The finding survives. Its proposed S[] is right under one answer of an open question, but it names the wrong question and gives an alternative that no definition produces.

THE FACTS HOLD. The E16 leaf's S[A-1KO] (besogo reads A-1KO+) is wrong.
- White takes at A18. Black must retake with a threat; otherwise B19 takes four stones and White lives.
- With one threat more than White, Black fails in both areas.

E16 NEEDS 3 THREATS UNDER THE OWNER'S c121 RULE (settled), WHICH KEEPS WHITE'S APPROACH-ROUND FREE MOVE OUT OF THE LABEL.
- Black needs one approach (A14 or F19).
- Black's next retake puts White in atari, and White answers locally: it extends at the other extendable liberty.
- Black must fill once more (G19, or A13/B14), and White retakes for free.
- A14 and F19 need only 2, because Black keeps E16 for the capture, and White can never extend there.
- By the full count all three need 4 (narrow area, all decided now; A14 is 4, not "3 or 4").
- So E16 is never better than its siblings. The research's two fixes alone would wrongly mark A14 and F19 wrong.

THE OPEN QUESTION IS QUESTION 3, NOT THE APPROACH-LABEL DECISION OR c121. Black's extra fill is "an approach after a local answer to a threatening capture", the c014 shape, and it passes D4's approach test.
- Read as an extra move inside the ko (D7 as written): A-1KO-2. Barring White's extension while it is under the ban drops the direct-ko value from 2 to 1.
- Read as an approach: A-2KO-. This is the design's proposed answer to question 3, and it fits the owner's wording "approaches to start a normal ko".
- Both labels need 3 threats.

NO READING GIVES E16 A-1KO-.
- The extension is White's answer to a threatening retake, not a free move of an approach round, so c121 keeps it in the count.
- The equal full count of 4 is the strict reading. It would put A-1KO-3 on all three leaves, which contradicts c121 and the siblings' A-1KO-.

GRADING (besogo's own code)
- Under either answer to question 3, only E16 at move 15 turns wrong.
- A14 (with W A18 under it) and F19 stay correct, A16 and C19 at move 5 stay correct, and the root becomes A-1KO-.
- E16 at A-1KO-, or all three at A-1KO-3, changes no mark.

KEY LINES. The finding's corrections hold in both areas: k027 must approach at A14 and k028 at F19, keeping E16 for the capture.

FOR THE OWNER. If he wants E16 to stay correct because all three need the same threats in real play, that would be a new decision against his own c121 rule. He should be shown it.

reviews.explanation:
The finding holds.

**The E16 leaf.** White takes at A18 at once. Black must retake with a threat, or B19 takes four stones and White lives. Black then needs one approach, at A14 or F19. Whichever of the two Black leaves for last, White extends there when Black's second retake puts it in atari: at A14 it gets A13 and B14, at F19 it gets F18 and G19. Black must answer, White retakes for free, and Black needs a third threat. That extension is White's local threat in the direct ko, so the leaf is A-1KO-2.

The tree's A-1KO is wrong in every reading: besogo reads it as A-1KO+, and Black fails even with one threat more than White.

**The siblings.** After A14 or F19 at move 15, Black approaches at the other extendable liberty. It keeps E16 for the capture, because White can never extend there. Both siblings are A-1KO-. The research's key lines approach at E16 and fail exactly as the finding says. The working approaches are A14 for k027 and F19 for k028.

**What I tried, without success:**
- A waiting move that removes one extension in advance (G19, F18, B14, A13), and every other waiting move.
- Both approach orders.
- A Black local threat.
- White alternatives to the take at A18. All of them let Black win with 3 threats, so A18 is White's only best move at all three nodes.

**The search left open.** The checker's own label run (A-1KO?, undecided at 14M nodes) and the grading checker both left one search open: Black's free move with one threat, in the wider area. It is now decided: every Black move fails.
- In the narrow area the split over Black's moves decides it with no bar.
- In the wider area I barred White, and only White, from far-off points; a bar on White alone can only help Black. Every waiting move then fails to White's free retake.
- Two structural checks also fit the label: the round is an approach, not a stage, and barring the extension while White is under the ban turns the direct ko back into a plain KO-.

**besogo's grading** matches the finding:
- With the research fixes alone, A14 and F19 at move 15 turn wrong.
- Adding E16 at A-1KO-2 turns only E16 wrong.
- Giving E16 the siblings' label changes nothing; so does A-1KO-3 for all three.
- E16 at A-2KO- grades the same as A-1KO-2.

**Two small corrections:**
1. The c121 approach-round rule is answered, not open, and under it E16 is A-1KO-2. The open part is question 4. Read by count, all three moves need exactly 4 in the narrow area, so each would be A-1KO-3, not A-1KO-. What matters for grading is only that E16 gets the same label as A14 and F19.
2. The full counts are settled only in the narrow area (4 each). In the wider area they stay undecided, even with one-sided bars and splits. There White can also capture a lone Black stone at A14 or F19 without making a second ko. So the finding's 'under no reading is E16 better' rests on the narrow counts and the labels.
